text:
GENERATE BURST KP-B1f — THE FALLEN CROSS, revision 1: more broken, split down its centre, lying flat (Run KC2-PLAY; conductor gandalf; Matt: "B - the cross. But probably even more broken; maybe a jagged crack down the center." It is now THE CENTRE OBJECT of the arena — the player stands and fights on it). task_id "KP-B1f".

WHAT THIS IS. ONE 1536x1024 image: a single object on a flat pure #00ff00 background — nothing else painted, no floor, no shadow, no context. IMAGE 1 is the previous version of this same object and it is right in glass, colour, ornament and iconography: KEEP all of that. Two things change.

CHANGE 1 — IT IS LYING FLAT ON THE FLOOR, seen from our fixed game camera: an elevated three-quarter view, 52.95 degrees down, north up-screen. IMAGE 1 drew it standing upright and facing us; that is wrong. Foreshorten it: 1 m across the screen = 100.6 px, 1 m up/down the screen = 80.3 px, so the cross is squashed vertically to about 0.8 of its width — a shape lying on the ground and seen from above and in front, not a shape hanging on a wall. Its long axis runs NORTH-SOUTH (up-down the screen), head of the cross toward the top. About 8 m tall, so roughly 640 px of screen height and 480 px across the arms. A 1.9 m person standing beside it would be 115 px tall (IMAGE 3).

CHANGE 2 — IT IS MUCH MORE BROKEN. It fell from a great height onto stone. A JAGGED CRACK SPLITS IT DOWN THE CENTRE, running the length of the long axis — the two halves are shifted slightly apart and out of plane, one side sitting a little higher than the other where it landed on rubble. Sections of stone tracery are snapped clean through and displaced; one arm of the cross is broken off and lying at an angle, still attached by a twist of lead; whole panes are gone, leaving empty leadwork like a torn net; shattered glass is scattered in a wide field around it, drifts of it along the crack; long splinters of glass and lead stand up out of the break. Still: MOST of the glass that remains is INTACT and VIVID — deep ruby, cobalt, emerald, amber, violet, gold, with the knight-saint, the sun and the chains still readable in the leadwork. The break should hurt to look at BECAUSE the thing is beautiful. Fresh breaks: clean edges, pale stone inside the fractures, grit and dust beside them — this fell a week ago, not a century ago.

LIGHT: the sun sets in the WEST (screen LEFT). A long gold sunset highlight rakes across the glass from the left; fire out of frame throws warm, flickering reflections that catch in the panes and in the standing splinters; the coloured glass glows where the light passes through it. This object is the most beautiful and the most violated thing in the room and the light should say both.

REGISTER: HAND-DRAWN painted 2D as in IMAGE 2 (our own level): confident dark contour with visible taper and varying weight, painted fills in clean planes, restrained texture, readable silhouettes; not pixel art, not cel-shaded, not a 3D render, not photoreal. The glass may glow.

PLATE RULE: everything that is not the cross and its scattered glass and stone is flat pure #00ff00 exactly — no shadow on the green, no floor, no haze. The object is cut out and placed on the painted floor later; its shadow and its flame-flicker are added by the scene.

DELIVER exactly ONE 1536x1024 image_gen result. ONE retry only if: it is drawn upright or unforeshortened instead of lying flat under our camera, the centre crack is missing, the background is not flat #00ff00, the glass is dull, or the register drifts from IMAGE 2 — name the reason. Copy the output from $CODEX_HOME/generated_images/... to out/window_B2_cross_broken.png with sha256. No code. No other files. No web.
RETURN: receipt task_id "KP-B1f"; images = the file with prompt, references and elapsed_s; calls_used = the TRUE number of image_gen calls; status; concerns listed honestly. Never PASS/FAIL.

references.role: IMAGE 1 — the previous cross: glass, colour, ornament and iconography are RIGHT; its upright pose and its light are what change
IMAGE 2 — register exemplar: our painted level (match the hand)
IMAGE 3 — scale figure: a 1.9 m person = 115 px (do not paint)
